title: Large Language Models are Zero-Shot Reasoners
authors: T. Kojima, S. Gu, M. Reid, Y. Matsuo, Y. Iwasawa
before: Chain of thought needed hand-written worked examples in the prompt.
problem: Writing exemplars for every task is laborious and task-specific.
breakthrough: A single phrase asking the model to think step by step, with no examples, unlocks most of the same gain.
why: It showed the reasoning behaviour was already in the model, waiting for a cue. Cheap, universal, and much copied.
next: Absorbed into system prompts everywhere, then trained in directly by reasoning models.
inherits: The instruction to reason before answering.
